subject.title: Device identity generation should not depend on browser Secure Context — breaks HTTP reverse-proxy deployments

question: Should browser Control UI device identity be allowed to generate and authenticate after the UI is delivered over remote plain HTTP, and if so should that be an explicit opt-in policy instead of the default?
rationale: The remaining change is not just replacing a hash helper; it decides whether persistent operator browser identity can be trusted when the page itself may have been modified in transit.

options.title: Keep secure-context requirement
options.body: Continue blocking remote plain-HTTP device identity and rely on HTTPS, localhost, trusted-proxy, break-glass, and warning/docs mitigations for self-hosted deployments.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in
options.body: Allow pure-JS browser identity only behind a clearly named insecure Control UI policy with security-audit coverage, docs, and tests for both default-blocked and opt-in behavior.

options.title: Allow by default
options.body: Remove the secure-context gate and WebCrypto digest dependency everywhere, accepting a broader remote-plaintext trust model for Control UI operators.

recommendation.title: Keep secure-context requirement
recommendation.body: Continue blocking remote plain-HTTP device identity and rely on HTTPS, localhost, trusted-proxy, break-glass, and warning/docs mitigations for self-hosted deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: The central remaining decision traces to the secure Control UI auth boundary introduced in f76e3c141927 and to current Gateway/UI auth policy ownership.
